title: Task Scheduler
summary: Find the least time to finish all tasks when equal tasks must be separated by a cooldown.

tests.explain: One valid schedule is A B idle A B idle A B: 8 time units. Each A and each B must wait two units before repeating.
No cooldown, so tasks run back to back: 6 units.
A is the bottleneck: A _ _ A _ _ A _ _ A _ _ A _ _ A needs 16 units, and the six other tasks fill 6 of the 10 gap slots, so 4 slots stay idle.

hints: Each time unit you run one task or sit idle. Two equal tasks need at least n other time units between them. Which task type is the bottleneck?

The most frequent task sets the schedule's skeleton: its copies are spaced n + 1 apart. Everything else can be dropped into the gaps, and if there are too few other tasks, the leftover gaps become idle time.

With maxCount the highest frequency and k the number of task types that share that frequency, the answer is max(tasks.length, (maxCount - 1) * (n + 1) + k). Alternatively, simulate with a max-heap of remaining counts and a queue of tasks cooling down.

complexity.time: O(T) with the counting formula (T tasks, at most 26 types); O(T log 26) with the heap simulation
